summary: The German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) is Germany's national funding body for international students. Its master's and doctoral scholarships pay a monthly stipend plus insurance and travel — and because most German public universities charge no tuition, that stipend effectively makes the whole degree funded.
covers: A monthly stipend of €992 for master's students and €1,300 for doctoral candidates (the rates DAAD lists on its scholarship overview; always check the current call).
Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance, and a travel allowance.
On the Study Scholarships for master's programmes: an annual study allowance of €460, plus a rent subsidy and family allowances on application.
Funded German language courses before or during your studies, with the TestDaF or DSH exam fee refunded.
Tuition is not paid by DAAD — but most public universities in Germany charge none.
eligibility: Each DAAD programme has its own country list. If your country is not listed in the call, you cannot apply to that programme.

Study Scholarships (master's): a completed first degree by the time funding starts, a degree no more than six years old at the application deadline, and no more than 15 months' residence in Germany at the deadline.
EPOS development-related postgraduate courses: graduates from eligible developing countries, usually with a four-year bachelor's and at least two years' professional experience.
Doctoral grants are open to candidates from nearly all countries; full doctoral programmes focus on developing and emerging countries.
how_to_apply: Search the DAAD scholarship database (funding-guide.de) with your nationality, level and subject, and open the call for the programme that fits.
Read the call's country-specific deadline — it differs by country and, for EPOS, by course.

Prepare a CV (up to three pages), a one-to-three-page motivation letter, transcripts, degree certificate, language certificate (no older than three years) and one recommendation letter from a university teacher.
Submit through the DAAD portal as PDFs, or — for EPOS — directly to the university course as its call instructs. The portal closes at midnight German time on the last day.
Shortlisted candidates may be interviewed; funding for master's study usually starts on 1 October of the following year.
watch_out: DAAD is many programmes, not one scholarship. Applying to the wrong call is the most common mistake.
Most calls close between August and November for study starting the following October — about a year ahead.
DAAD never charges application fees and never contacts applicants through social media. See our guide to [spotting scholarship scams]({{root}}guides/scholarship-scams/).
EPOS applications go through the individual course, which sets its own deadline — often 15 October or earlier.
